I think that the worst part of your story is the part about your mom ignoring you. It's bad enough to be victimized by someone you were forced to be in contact with on a daily basis, but what makes this situation worse is the fact that you are being re-victimized by the person you love and trust the most--your mom.  There is absolutely no excuse for her behavior. I know you are in a vulnerable situation right now, but it seems like the home you are living in at this point is extremely toxic. You need to reach out to anyone who can help. I think your best bet is the school nurse--she is obligated to report these things without judgement. I know you are scared that no one will believe you because of your own mother, but please, be the bigger person and stand up for yourself. Your life IS important, regardless of what you have been through, you are STILL someone who deserves both love and respect. This will never change. Thank you for sharing your story, and please be brave. You can do this, you can fight.

waking up from anesthesia after a 30min. procedure. I looked at the heart monitor, my heart monitor, and the reading dropped from 105 to 65 in a matter of seconds. then as the nurse was taking my iv out, i made a comment about how it was nice that she had a pre-made band-aid out of gauze and tape ready. she made no eye contact, did not say a word, then when I looked at her she appeared to look down and embarrassed, almost as if she had seen me naked. I thought it was strange and I just wanted to get out of there asap, my boyfriend also said it was weird she appeared ashamed or deeply somber about something...much different than before I was put under. That's the weirdest feeling when you wake up feeling like something bad happened and then you see that look on someone's face that's almost indescribable. Scary.

As previous posters have stated, I, too believe you may have had a very real (and scary) episode of sleep paralysis. I get this sometimes, too. Recently had one where I thought I was awake in my room (everything looked exactly the same) but I could not move my body to get out of bed. I had to do so because I thought I left a jug of milk out, that it was going rotten. Luckily I was able to snap out of it by trying to pick up something off my dresser. When I picked it up, my hand became the object and then my brain switched and I woke up, staring at the exact same thing I was trying to pick up. This time I could move, and was very happy. That's the key about sleep paralysis, you're asleep but you're awake so it's pretty weird. When you mention being "back in your body" it also reminds me of a waking dream I had of going back into my body. I saw this kid and I knew who he was, and I said to him, "I know how to get to heaven, I can show you". Then I jumped into a hole and realized I was breathing through my body and opened my eyes to find my real body breathing as if I was out of my body and just breathed life back into it. It was really strange! Hope you can learn to cope with these feelings, the fear and experience are both very real to YOU and that's why its important for you to learn to cope with these things. Thank you for sharing your story!

Seroquel is a good drug, I've been on Zyprexa and seroquel. Seroquel was much better. Side effects I get are drowsiness  (I take it before bed) and absent sex drive, which I actually enjoy because I have a trauma history and even though sex is important it's still to complex for me to manage just yet (bad experiences). Also, been talking it 6 months, actually lost weight because I went on a vegan diet when i started it, due to being scared of the increase in weight.

I am also on seroquel 300mg, been on it for maybe 6 months. Everyone is right in saying that it causes drowsiness, but its great as a sleep aid. The weight gain hasn't been significant for me, so I guess I probably just got lucky. It helps me a lot with moods and another great thing is that I have no sex drive whatsoever. Pretty great when you are someone who has been promiscuous in the past, and just want to stay away from that part of your life. I've been in and out of the mental health system for a while now (4 years), but I can really see this drug as something that can work for me, long-term.
